name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Wasserman Schultz with large financial advantage ($1.9M cash)
Republican challenger raised only ~$64K with minimal outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~94%
model.rationale: The baseline's Safe D rating rests on a D+20 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a severely underfunded Republican challenger, with Polymarket corroborating at 94%. I shade the margin slightly below the 24.8 baseline given no polling and the unusual incumbent transition, but well within the Safe D band.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected well-funded outside spending against Wasserman Schultz could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
This South Florida seat is solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about D+20. Debbie Wasserman Schultz, a long-serving incumbent, enters the general election with a dominant financial position: over $3.3 million raised and $1.9 million on hand. Her Republican opponent, Brent Andersen, has raised roughly $64,000, and an independent candidate trails far behind in both money and profile.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast leans on fundamentals, which point strongly to the incumbent. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 94% chance of holding the seat. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling and the unusual circumstances of the seat change earlier in the cycle, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
